newsitem.title: USA: India may need to import one mln T wheat - US Wheat.
newsitem.headline: India may need to import one mln T wheat - US Wheat.

text.p: Argentina is the major force at the moment in the world wheat market and is expected to export a record 10 million tonnes of wheat this marketing year, a major U.S. wheat growers group said Wednesday.
In a briefing on the world wheat outlook, U.S. Wheat Associates research and marketing analyst Gregg Doud also predicted India may need to import one million tonnes of wheat in the coming months,

Doud said Argentina has been pricing its wheat lower than its competitors because the country has very limited storage capability for the large crop forecast, has no grade established on the grain and is at a disadvantage on freight.
"Think of it more as a clearance sale, they've got to push it out the door," he said.
"They are probably the major force in determining what's going on in the world right now with regard to wheat, Australia's a very close second," Doud said.
He noted Canada and Australia had been "really duking it out" for wheat business in Latin America in recent weeks.

Doud predicted those two countries would be very aggressive in the months ahead because both are forecast to have large ending stocks on hand. "In the summer of 1997, we're going to be facing a lot of competition in Australia and Canada who traditionally have ending stocks lower...but are still going to have wheat for sale facing us in a new crop situation," said Paul Dickerson, vice president of grower group who also spoke to the briefing. The U.S. is not a player at the moment in the world wheat market, Doud said, because farmers resisting selling and strong domestic demand have pushed prices up. "We're not in the game at the present time for an old crop situation," he said. Doud said India "may have to do something in the world wheat market in short order" in the face of rising consumption and skyrocketing domestic wheat prices. Asked specifically about rumours India might be seeking 1.0 million tonnes of wheat, he said its "a very real possibility."
